answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can transact, with the stake recorded in a shared atlas of verified participants. A newcomer earns trust slowly: early trades are capped, and honest behavior over time raises its standing, while detected fraud forfeits the stake. Like a tide, this makes flooding the network expensive, since an attacker must fund every fake identity and risks losing each deposit, while legitimate agents, sustained by the nectar of real earned reputation, keep operating cheaply.
